oliver: Heads-up — saw a double-apply + stale-read combo during a rebalance where eviction credits and lease renewal overlapped. Short log: 

```
[2026-08-03T12:00:01Z] lease-renew: prefix=acct11/cart lease_id=L:300 -> renewed
[2026-08-03T12:00:01Z] evict-credit-transfer: from=nodeA to=nodeB prefix=acct11/cart credits=1
[2026-08-03T12:00:02Z] apply@nodeA: put k=acct11/cart:item7 v=2 op_guid=op:aa123 -> ok
[2026-08-03T12:00:02Z] takeover-ack@nodeB: accepted lease L:301 (from L:300)
[2026-08-03T12:00:02Z] read@nodeB: k=acct11/cart:item7 -> v=1 (stale)
```

paula: Interesting. So nodeA applied then credits moved and nodeB accepted takeover quickly. Did nodeB prefill?

oliver: No prefill, we were testing fast-credit-transfer to reduce downtime. The lease handover path accepted the new lease and flipped ownership, but nodeB's cache missed the recent put.

zhen: This looks like two orthogonal races: (1) lease/ownership switch without durable checkpoint of last_seq, (2) credit-transfer path that skipped waiting for in-flight applies to quiesce. Together they allow shadowing: nodeB thinks it's owner but doesn't see nodeA's latest in-memory state.

mina: We've seen shadowing before in other forms, but usually the token schema covered it. Here the credit-transfer optimization bypassed some of that. We need to check invariants: takeover should guarantee visibility of all acknowledged writes up to some sequence.

paula: Agree. Options: (A) make credit-transfer block until old owner quiesces or persists last_seq; (B) accept fast transfer but mark prefix on new owner as "shadowed" and forward reads until a confirmation ack is observed; (C) make per-op idempotency via op_guid such that duplicate apply harmlessly dedupes on replay. Tradeoffs?

zhen: (C) is good general hygiene but doesn't fix stale reads — it prevents double-apply but not the visibility gap. (A) keeps correctness but hurts transfer latency. (B) seems balanced: fast transfer + short read forwarding. But we need a robust handshake so that the new owner knows the watermark to wait for.

oliver: How about hybrid: during credit-transfer, old owner includes a transfer-checkpoint {last_durable_seq, last_op_guids_snapshot, transfer_id} which is appended to a tiny metadata commit. New owner accepts transfer_id and marks prefix=shadowed until it has observed >=last_durable_seq or received confirm from old owner. Meanwhile, reads are forwarded or trigger a one-shot delta-fetch using transfer_id.

mina: We'll need to ensure last_op_guids_snapshot is small — only recent op_guids or a Bloom of guids — because keeping long lists is expensive. Bloom could give false positives (we'd dedupe perhaps unnecessarily) but better than nothing.

paula: Also consider per-key versioning: keep an apply-epoch in the cache entry (owner_epoch, op_seq). On takeover, new owner refuses to serve entries with owner_epoch < transfer_epoch unless catch-up done. That pushes logic into fast-path cache checks but avoids per-read RPCs in steady state.

zhen: Implementation sketch combining ideas:
- On credit-transfer initiate: old owner writes tiny transfer-checkpoint = {transfer_id, last_durable_seq, bloom_recent_op_guids} to local meta-store (durable append)
- New owner accepts transfer_id and sets prefix.state=shadowed with expected_seq=last_durable_seq
- New owner applies normal reads: if local entry.owner_epoch < transfer_epoch OR local_seq < expected_seq -> do one-shot delta fetch from old owner or sequencer; if fetch fails within 150ms, forward read to sequencer as fallback
- Also keep op_guid dedupe on apply to avoid double-apply if deltas arrive twice
- Expose telemetry: transfer-checkpoint-latency, shadowed-prefix-rate, delta-fetch-latency, forwarded-read-rate

oliver: That sounds reasonable. Key tradeoffs: extra small durable writes on transfer (but amortizable), added fast-path epoch check (cheap branch), and occasional delta-fetch stalls on first reads. All gate behind FF for canary.

mina: Operator plan: roll out on canary with low churn, monitor forwarded-read-rate and shadowed-prefix-rate. If transfer-checkpoint IO spikes too high during eviction storms, we can switch to batched-transfer-checkpoints for multi-prefix transfers.

paula: One more safety net: if shadowed state persists > X seconds, trigger async full prefill and alert. We'll need an escape hatch feature toggle to force serial transfers for a cluster if too noisy.
devops-bot: Created issue RM-9900: "credit-transfer-shadowing-handshake" assigned to oliver & zhen. :white_check_mark:

oliver: I'll write an RFC PR with the transfer-checkpoint schema and the cache-epoch quick-check. Will include microbench numbers for transfer latency and delta-fetch RTT. Thanks all. :pray:
